title: Populism, disinformation and Covid-19: Jair Bolsonaro's communication on Twitter
screen_reason: Content analysis of Jair Bolsonaro's 100 most-retweeted tweets (1 Jan 2020 - 30 Jun 2021) reports a quantitative share of items classified as disinformation with a stated denominator: 19 of the 100 most-retweeted tweets (19%) appeared on the Agencia Aos Fatos fact-check list as disinformation, and 13 of the 41 pandemic-related tweets in that set were disinformation. Falsity is judged against an external ground truth (a fact-checking agency), so this is CONTENT, not QUALITY.

estimates.date: 1 January 2020 - 30 June 2021 (tweets); retweets collected from 27 March 2020
estimates.measure_type: % of Jair Bolsonaro's 100 most-retweeted tweets that were flagged as containing disinformation
estimates.denominator: 100 most-retweeted tweets posted by @jairbolsonaro between 1 Jan 2020 and 30 Jun 2021 (drawn from 3,136 original tweets in the period)
estimates.definition: The tweet appeared in the Agencia Aos Fatos fact-checking agency's survey as content containing disinformation; the authors then typed each such tweet with Wardle & Derakhshan's information-disorder categories (predominantly 'conteudo enganoso' / misleading content, remainder manipulated content)
estimates.misinfo_def: "Desinformacao intencional (Disinformation): ... o conteudo de um tuite com informacoes falsas, equivocadas, imprecisas ou enganosas que sao compartilhadas de maneira intencional para causar danos" [Intentional disinformation: the content of a tweet with false, mistaken, inaccurate or misleading information shared intentionally to cause harm]
estimates.source_quote: Dentre as publicações com maior número de retuítes, 19 mensagens estavam no levantamento da Agência Aos Fatos11 como conteúdos contendo desinformação.
estimates.page_loc: Resultados, 'Discurso Populista' subsection (p. 255) and Consideracoes finais (p. 256)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Disinformation status was taken from the Brazilian fact-checking agency Agencia Aos Fatos' existing list, not coded by the authors ('optou-se por utilizar a classificacao ja realizada e validada pela agencia de Fact Check' / 'we chose to use the classification already made and validated by the fact-checking agency'). Four coders then applied the Wardle & Derakhshan typology to the flagged tweets, with annotations settled by discussion and majority vote in a final iteration. No inter-coder reliability statistic is reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: Para a analise de conteudo, o conjunto de dados foi limitado aos 100 textos mais retuitados. Optou-se por esse recorte uma vez que este trabalho investiga principalmente a narrativa publica em torno da comunicacao do presidente Jair Bolsonaro e os tuites que recebem um escrutinio consideravel oferecem um padrao razoavel. [For the content analysis the dataset was limited to the 100 most retweeted texts.] // Footnote 11: Dentre os 100 tweets mais retuitados, podem haver outros que nao foram classificados como desinformacao pela Agencia Aos Fatos. [Among the 100 most retweeted tweets there may be others that were not classified as disinformation by Aos Fatos.]
estimates.notes: Denominator is one named actor's own output, so CONTENT per the governing rule (it is a share of the tweets he posted, not of what was shared or seen). denom_selection is coded single_source (one account), but the set is ALSO rank-truncated to the top 100 by retweets, i.e. curated - an adjudicator may prefer denom_selection=curated. The truncation is a strong upward-selection risk: the paper itself shows the most-retweeted tweets are unrepresentative of all 3,136 tweets (hydroxychloroquine tweets are 1.72% of all tweets but 9% of the most-retweeted). Footnote 11 warns the 19% is a lower bound (only Aos Fatos-checked tweets count). Data collection spans Jan 2020-Jun 2021; year coded 2020 as the modal/midpoint year of the window. Country/language: article in Portuguese. source_quote is the exact Portuguese span from the text file (the trailing '11' after 'Aos Fatos' is the footnote marker as printed); other quoted fields are ASCII-transliterated with English translations in brackets. Translation of the source quote: 'Among the posts with the highest number of retweets, 19 messages were in the Agencia Aos Fatos survey as content containing disinformation.'

estimates.measure_type: % of Bolsonaro's most-retweeted pandemic-related tweets that contained disinformation
estimates.denominator: 41 of the 100 most-retweeted @jairbolsonaro tweets that dealt with the pandemic (37 with the pandemic as the main theme plus 4 with it as a secondary theme)
estimates.definition: The pandemic-related tweet appeared on the Agencia Aos Fatos disinformation list; 13 of the 19 flagged tweets were about the pandemic
estimates.misinfo_def: "Desinformacao intencional (Disinformation): ... informacoes falsas, equivocadas, imprecisas ou enganosas que sao compartilhadas de maneira intencional para causar danos" [false, mistaken, inaccurate or misleading information shared intentionally to cause harm]
estimates.source_quote: Por fim, cabe destacar que, dos 19 conteúdos mais retuitados e apontados como desinformação, 13 tratavam sobre a pandemia. Em outras palavras, é elucidar que, dos 41 conteúdos tratando de pandemia, mais de 30% apresentam desinformação.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same procedure as the 19% row: Agencia Aos Fatos fact-check list for the disinformation flag; four authors coded theme and Brennen et al. (2020) Covid narrative type; no reliability statistic reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: Entre os tweets mais retuitados, 37 tratam especificamente da pandemia; tambem foram encontrados quatro tuites que tinham esse tema como secundario. Para este conjunto (41 casos), classificamos qual o posicionamento adotado. [Among the most retweeted tweets, 37 deal specifically with the pandemic; four more had this as a secondary theme. For this set (41 cases) we classified the stance adopted.]
estimates.notes: Kept under R8: 13 and 41 are both verbatim counts with the same denominator, so 13/41 = 31.7% is an exact part/whole share (the paper's own rounded phrasing is 'mais de 30%'). This is a topic subset of the same 100-tweet corpus, not a stricter definition, so definition_variant=false. Confidence medium because the 41 mixes tweets with the pandemic as the main theme (37) and as a secondary theme (4), and the same top-100 rank truncation applies. denom_scope=topical (a single-issue subset). Translation of source_quote: 'Finally, it is worth noting that of the 19 most-retweeted contents flagged as disinformation, 13 dealt with the pandemic. In other words, of the 41 contents dealing with the pandemic, more than 30% present disinformation.'

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) 63.16% of the 19 disinformation tweets were 'conteudo enganoso' (misleading content), the rest manipulated content, and the Brennen et al. breakdown of the 13 pandemic disinformation tweets (69.23% criticism of public authorities, 23.08% false information about medicines/symptoms/treatment, 7.69% criticism of prominent actors) - these are type breakdowns computed INSIDE the misinformation-only set (within_misinfo_content), and are typology shares rather than falsity shares, so omitted under R4. (b) 78% of the 100 most-retweeted tweets contained a populist element and 93% an emotional frame - populism/emotion, not misinformation. (c) 21.95% of the 41 pandemic tweets promoted remedies and treatments such as hydroxychloroquine, described by the authors as 'remedio comprovadamente sem eficacia' [a drug proven to be ineffective]; this is a stance category, not a falsity coding against a ground truth, so not extracted, though an adjudicator could argue it is a broader-definition variant of the covid row. (d) 13.27% (54/407) of pandemic tweets mentioned hydroxychloroquine and 1.72% of all 3,136 tweets did - topic-model classifications with no veracity judgement. (e) The topic-model shares in Tables 2 and 3 are theme shares, not misinformation shares.

rob.design: Census of one account: 3,136 original tweets, 488 replies and 244 retweets from @jairbolsonaro, 1 Jan 2020 - 30 Jun 2021, collected with the Twitter API v2 and the Twint library (retweets only from 27 Mar 2020 because of the API's 3,200-item cap). Level 1: unsupervised topic modelling with BERTimbau (50 topics; 1,979 of 3,136 tweets, 63.11%, classifiable, 1,157 left as 'Others'). Level 2: manual content analysis by four coders of the 100 most-retweeted tweets, coding populism (Bobba 2018), emotional frame (Ekman) and information disorder (Wardle & Derakhshan; Brennen et al. for Covid narratives); disagreements settled by discussion and majority vote at the final iteration; the authors acknowledge susceptibility to human bias; NO inter-coder reliability statistic (kappa or percent agreement) is reported. Disinformation status itself was not coded by the authors but imported from the Agencia Aos Fatos fact-check list, which the authors note may under-count (footnote 11). No sampling of users and no response rate (platform data).

[Intentional disinformation: this term refers to the content of a tweet with false, mistaken, inaccurate or misleading information shared intentionally to cause harm.]
